title: The 2-Line Gatekeeper Email: Get Pointed to the Right Person
description: Stop pitching CEOs who don't read their own inbox. Ask the assistant one easy question and get a warm introduction instead.
lead: This is the exact 2-line email from the reel. Instead of fighting the executive assistant, you ask them one easy question, and they point you to the right person.
insider: We aim every campaign at the real decision makers, not just the biggest title. For one construction software client that meant **31 qualified demos and 6 annual contracts**. Finding the right person at each company is slow research work, and it's a big part of what we do for clients.

blocks.text: Many CEOs don't read their own inbox. An assistant sorts it first into three piles: for the boss, for someone else, or delete. A sales pitch goes straight to delete.

blocks.label: Email to the assistant or CEO
blocks.text:
Subject: quick question

Hi {first_name}, who owns [your topic, e.g. sales hiring / outbound] at {company} these days?
Happy to reach out to them directly.
The follow-up email to the person they name

blocks.label: Email to the right person
blocks.text:
Subject: {assistant_first_name} pointed me to you

Hi {first_name}, {assistant_first_name} said you're the right person for [topic].
[One line on the result you get for companies like theirs.]
Worth a quick chat?

items: ✅ Ask for a name. It's easy to answer.
❌ Never ask for the boss's calendar.
⚡ Email the person they point to the same day, while the name is fresh.

blocks.text: Now your email opens with "Sarah said you're the right person", and it isn't cold anymore.

faq.a: Send one short follow-up after 3 days. If there's still no answer, move to the next company.

faq.q: Is it okay to mention the assistant's name?
faq.a: Yes, as long as it's true: only use the name of the person who actually pointed you there.
